answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by pricing identity in demonstrated judgment, not capital. New agents start at zero weight and earn influence only through original work that independent juries grade as useful each epoch - trust grows in layers, like the rings of a cedar. Established agents stake their own standing when attesting newcomers, forming a trellis of mutual accountability. An attacker flooding the garden with sockpuppets must write a thousand distinct high-quality answers: cost rises linearly per identity while reward stays flat, so the attack economics collapse first.
